sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2010. Change Request 2010-026 (submitted by Sara Van Cott, SIL-PNG): reference name [nib] Nakama -> Nakame; adopted 2011-05-18.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Name change only ('Nakame is the spelling which most closely represents the pronunciation of most speakers'); cites the unpublished Potter, Gray & Retsema 2006 'Nakame [nib] Language Survey Report' (ms., Ukarumpa: SIL). No stress statement.

sources.citation: Smith, Geoffrey P. 1988. Morobe counting systems. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 26, 1-132. Pacific Linguistics A-76.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 67 (pp. 88-89): numerals of the Northern and Southern dialects of Nakama, Erap Family; nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: McElhanon, K.A. 1984. A linguistic field guide to the Morobe Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-57.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Village list only: Nakama (67) pop. 1,036; North dialect (Kwaipunum, Sikeran, Sokam), South dialect (Dzensan, Pupuf, Wasin). Lists SIL teams for Numanggang (Hynum) and Urii (Webb) but none for Nakama. No phonology.

sources.citation: McElhanon, K.A. 1975. North-eastern Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 527-567. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology sec. 2.8.1.4.1 (pp. 544-546) tabulates phonemes of ten representative languages (Kâte, Ono, Selepet, Kube, Nabak, Urii, Wantoat, Kewieng, Rawa, Kovai), not Nakama, and does not mention stress at all. Nakama (ER-24, p. 536): villages and the h ~ s dialect correspondence only.

sources.citation: Claassen, Oren R. & Kenneth A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 11, 45-78. Pacific Linguistics A-23. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 6.1 (pp. 63-66) gives phoneme inventories for Rawa, Yupna, Uruwa, Wantoat and Uri only; the single stress sentence (p. 66) is 'Stress is phonemic in Rawa but probably sub-phonemic in Yupna and Wantoat. In none of these languages does it carry a heavy functional load.' Nakama (sec. 2.7.9, pp. 56-57) gets only population, location and two dialects (N/S, 87% cognate). Nothing on Nakama stress.

sources.citation: Hooley, Bruce A. & Kenneth A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Morobe District, New Guinea. In S.A. Wurm & D.C. Laycock (eds), Pacific linguistic studies in honour of Arthur Capell, 1065-1094. Pacific Linguistics C-13.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Classification/lexicostatistics only. p. 1073: Nakama west of Boana, two dialects, northern s corresponds to southern h; 55% with Nek, 65% with Numanggang; Nuk-Nek-Nakama-Numanggang-Munkip form a sub-family of the Erap Family. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page naka1264 (Hammarström et al.)
sources.note: Lists only Hooley & McElhanon 1970 pp. 1072-1073 ('Comments on subclassification') and Ethnologue 2025 for endangerment (6b Threatened). No descriptive reference of any kind.
Stub; cites Ethnologue only (1,600 speakers, 2006). No phonology.

sources.citation: Hynum, David. 2010/1995. Numanggang phonology / Numanggang grammar essentials (SIL-PNG manuscripts); Webb, Thomas. 1974-. Urii phonology (SIL-PNG).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Closest described relatives (Numanggang 65% cognate with Nakama, same Erap sub-family; Urii in the same family). Not statements about Nakama, but the only phonological descriptions of the sub-family; useful only for a family-level note, never as a catalog entry for naka1264.
